findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the following food contact surfaces to contain an accumulation of debris:
1) A knife hanging in ready to use position in the kitchen.
2) The ice scoop holder at the server station.
CORRECTED- items were brought to the main kitchen dish machine for ware-washing.
Ensure food contact surfaces are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency to remain clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the multiple dish machines failing to meet sanitizing requirements:
1) The heat sanitizing restaurant dish machine reached 153F after four runs. The facility consulted their engineer to check the heat boosters. A follow up inspection is scheduled for 7/10 to verify that the machine is reaching a minimum heat sanitizing temperature of 160F.
2) FIRST REPEAT: The chemical sanitizing dish machine at the Globe was dispensing 0 ppm sanitizer. CORRECTED- the machine was primed multiple times and the dish machine was observed to be dispensing 50 ppm Chlorine. 
Dishes produced in the restaurant should must be brought to the main kitchen dish machine for proper ware washing until the machine is serviced. Ensure all dish machines are tested frequently to verify that the machine is reaching the sanitizing concentration (or a minimum temperature of 160F) as recommended by the manufacturer's label.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed a gallon of milk and creamer without date marking at the bar reach in cooler. CORRECTED- the PIC could not guarantee the date these items were opened, and discarded them as a result. Ensure that date marking happens within 24 hours of opening a TCS (time/temperature controlled for safety) food. To identify TCS foods, look for the phrases “refrigerate after opening” or “keep refrigerated” on the item packaging. Additionally, anything prepared in the kitchen that is not shelf-stable must also be date marked within 24 hours of preparation.

Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the hot holding unit at the front of the kitchen to have a piece of duct tape on it, and the gaskets to be in disrepair. The PIC removed the duct tape and stated they will be ordering new gaskets. Ensure all nonfood contact surfaces are maintained to be smooth and easily cleanable to prevent the deterioration of equipment into ready to eat foods.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Inspector observed two areas to have soiled food-contact surfaces. Both areas were at the detached Globe Tavern. The first area is the drain-tube connected to the soda gun holder. The tube has a build-up of soils in the tube. A reusable straw brush could be a good tool for cleaning this. The second area is the ice scoop holder at the bar. The scoop holder has a build-up of soils along the bottom edges. The scoop comes directly into contact with these soils when the scoop is inserted in the holder. Ensure both of these areas are cleaned regularly enough to keep them clean. They also require regular sanitization, as they are a food-contact surface (ice and soda are both considered food).

Inspector will return 09/18/25 to re-inspect the condition of these areas.

Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

To identify TCS foods, look for the phrases “refrigerate after opening” or “keep refrigerated” on the item packaging. Additionally, anything prepared in the kitchen that is not shelf-stable must also be date marked within 24 hours of preparation. Should staff have any date-marking questions, call me at (217) 341-2603.

Inspector will return 09/18/25 to re-inspect date marking practices.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a cart of clean dishes being stored under the EcoLab pest-control light in the dish room. Discussed placement of dishes with PIC. PIC removed the cart and placed it in a covered area where dishes will be safe from contamination. Ensure that no food or food-contact surfaces are stored under pest control devices.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (A) Insect control devices that are used to electrocute or stun flying insects shall be designed to retain the insect within the device. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an area of the floor in the kitchen to be in disrepair. PIC informed inspector that a piece of equipment had just been removed from the area, and the facility is currently looking for a replacement. Inspector observed the floor sealant to be broken and removed from around a drain on the floor. This will need to be patched to render the surface smooth and easily cleanable. Inspector also noticed that there was a gap between the wall and floor in this area. Ensure this gap is sealed to prevent pest entry, and also to make the surface transition smooth and easily cleanable.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: Inspector observed the area inside of the ice machine to be soiled. Maintenance is currently cleaning inside of the ice machine. The violation is considered corrected on site. Protect all food from potential contamination 
(A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.112: Upon arrival the conveyor dish machine had an alarm sign on the display and the final rinse temperature gauge was sitting at 120F. The dish washer noted that the booster heater had not been turned on. The booster was turned on and the final rinse temperature gauge came up to over 189F quickly. A maximum registering thermometer was run and the dish machine is now sanitizing at 158F. Ensure that staff are properly trained for the job they are performing. The violation was corrected on site. 
(A) Temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse may not be more than 194F or less than 165F for stationary rack, single temperature machines. All other machines can be no less than 180F. (B) Maximum temperature does not apply to high pressure and temperature systems with wand-type spraying devices.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
3-501.13: Inspector found 11 portions of ROP fish thawed in the 2 door cooler still in the packaging. Package read remove from packaging before thawing. The fish portions were discarded in the garbage. Thaw foods properly.

TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-904.11: A drawer holding utensils at a the kitchen utensil storage area is soiled. The drawer was removed and drawer including all of the utensils was given to dish for cleaning. Maintain this area free of accumulated soil. 
(A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser.

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed an area of floor in the back by cooking kettle to hold water and soil. Clean and repair the floor so that it does not hold water. Maintain floor clean and dry. Also the walls on either side of the small dish room are in disrepair. Tile at the floor is broken and missing. Repair the walls according to code. 

6-201.13: (A) floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1mm (one thirty-second inch). (B) Floors in which water flush cleaning methods are used shall be provided with drains and be graded to drain. Floor and wall junctures shall be coved and SEALED.
